title: Six-figure grid reference practice sheet with key
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y7 lesson 12 (Six-figure grid reference practice sheet with key (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 12: Landforms of glacial deposition and six-figure grid references. To understand how glaciers deposit moraine and drumlins and how to locate them with grid references

model.title: A drumlin is 3 tenths across square 2541 and 7 tenths up. Six-figure reference?

questions.q: A feature is 6 tenths across square 3417 and 2 tenths up. Six-figure reference?
questions.model: Easting: 34 then 6 tenths: 346. Northing: 17 then 2 tenths: 172. Together: 346172.

questions.a: Unsorted rock and clay dropped by ice

questions.q: Which end of a drumlin faces the way the ice came from?
Core: Draw and label a valley glacier showing lateral, medial and terminal moraine, then a field of drumlins after the ice melted.
questions.a: Correctly placed moraines; drumlins shown as egg shapes with blunt ends up-valley
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: two glaciers joining, a dark line where they meet labelled 'medial moraine'.

questions.q: Extend: Give six-figure grid references for three features on the OS extract worksheet.
questions.a: Answers on the worksheet key (each to the nearest tenth of a square)

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how an erratic can tell us the direction the ice moved.
questions.a: Its rock type matches a source area; the line from the source to where it lies shows the ice direction

questions.q: Big question: where does all the rock a glacier carries end up?
questions.a: It is deposited as moraine, drumlins and erratics when the ice melts
